Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Corp. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to John Smith, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy Corp.'s Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are David Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Rodriguez, Chief Operating Officer; Lisa Chen, VP of Exploration; Tom Harris, VP of Marketing; and Emily Green, Chief Sustainability Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to David Thompson.

David Thompson: Thank you, John, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy Corp. delivered solid results in Q3 2024, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved robust production growth and meaningful free cash flow generation. I'm particularly pleased with our progress on deleveraging the balance sheet while maintaining capital discipline. We are focused on high-return development in our core basins. Further, we are working on optimizing our hedging to protect downside while capturing upside. We continue to adjust to market volatility through prudent capital allocation. We are advancing our exploration portfolio with high-potential prospects. Finally, we are taking steps to enhance sustainability across operations.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you, David. As David mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $5.4 billion, up 15% year-over-year. Operating income was $1.9 billion, and net income was $1.3 billion. We generated $1.8 billion in free cash flow and returned $900 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $14.8 billion in total debt and $2.1 billion in cash.

Good afternoon, everyone. As we dive into our balance sheet strength—a key pillar of our strategy in this volatile commodity environment—I'll provide a detailed update on our total debt, net debt position, and leverage metrics. Our disciplined capital allocation has continued to deliver meaningful deleveraging, positioning us exceptionally well amid Brent crude averaging $82 per barrel this quarter and WTI holding steady around $78, supported by healthy global demand and OPEC+ discipline.

Starting with total debt, we ended the quarter at $14.8 billion, down from $16.2 billion at year-end 2023 and a sharp reduction from the $20.1 billion peak in Q4 2022 during the post-pandemic recovery. This reflects our proactive approach to high-grading our debt portfolio. Breakdown by instrument: our revolving credit facility stands at a minimal $450 million drawn out of a $3.5 billion commitment—thanks to robust liquidity from operations—while term loans total $4.2 billion, primarily our 2021 Term Loan B maturing in 2028 at SOFR plus 200 bps. The bulk, $10.15 billion, is in fixed-rate senior unsecured notes, with a blended coupon of 4.8%. Notably, we completed a $1.2 billion tender offer in August, retiring higher-cost 6.5% notes due 2026 issued during the 2020 downturn, replaced by opportunistic issuance of 4.25% notes due 2031 at a yield below 4.5%. This refinancing shaved about 50 bps off our average cost of debt, now at 4.6%, and extends maturities out to an average of 7.2 years, with no major principal payments until 2027.

Moving to net debt, we calculate this as total debt less cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments. With $2.1 billion in unrestricted cash—bolstered by $1.8 billion in Q3 free cash flow generation—and an additional $400 million in marketable securities, our net debt stands at $12.3 billion, a 24% year-over-year decline. This metric is particularly relevant in our industry, as it accounts for our strong liquidity buffer amid production disruptions or price downside risks. For context, our Permian Basin assets alone generated $1.2 billion in FCF this quarter at current strip prices, underscoring the quality of our Tier 1 inventory.

On leverage ratios, we're proud of our progress toward our long-term target of 1.5x net debt to LTM EBITDA. At quarter-end, our net debt to LTM EBITDA ratio improved to 2.4x from 3.1x in Q3 2023 and 4.2x two years ago. LTM EBITDA came in at $5.15 billion, driven by upstream realizations of $45 per BOE net to our portfolio, with upstream EBITDA margins expanding to 62% on cost efficiencies in the Permian and Bakken. Our gross debt to EBITDA is 2.9x, and debt to book capitalization sits comfortably at 28%, well below peers like Occidental at 35% or Pioneer pre-merger levels around 40%. Covenant headroom under our RBL is robust at 3.5x EBITDA cushion, with elected commitments stress-tested to $60 WTI.

Regionally, this deleveraging is fueled by high-return assets. In the Permian Basin, where we hold 450,000 net acres with 2.5 MMBOE PDP reserves, Q3 production hit 220,000 BOE/d at $10/BOE LOE—our lowest ever—driving $800 million in levered FCF and enabling $500 million in debt paydown. Bakken volumes grew 8% QoQ to 85,000 BOE/d, with breakevens under $45 WTI, while our North Sea clipper assets benefited from Brent premia, though UK fiscal changes prompted a $200 million JV partner buy-in to accelerate decommissioning reserves. Emerging upside in Guyana-style offshore blocks off Namibia—where our recent farm-down to TotalEnergies unlocked $300 million in non-op carry—further diversifies cash flows without incremental leverage.

Strategically, we've executed several initiatives to sustain this trajectory. First, capex discipline: Q3 upstream capex was $900 million, 15% below guidance, focused on long laterals averaging 12,000 feet in the Delaware Basin with 95%+ frac intensity, yielding 20%+ IRR at $70 WTI. Second, hedging: 65% of 2025 oil volumes hedged at $75 floor via collars and fixed swaps, insulating EBITDA from volatility akin to 2022's swings. Third, asset optimization: We monetized $1.5 billion in non-core midstream and downstream assets YTD, including a nat gas processing plant sale mirroring Enterprise Products' model, recycling proceeds into buybacks and a 12% dividend hike. Looking forward, we guide to net debt/EBITDA below 2.0x by YE 2025, funded by $6-7 billion in annual FCF at $75+ oil, with bolt-on M&A potential in the $2-3 billion range—think Anadarko-style tuck-ins in the Eagle Ford.

In summary on the balance sheet, our debt profile is investment-grade caliber, with flexibility for growth or shareholder returns in any macro scenario.

As we wrap up our financial overview, I'd like to dive into our capital allocation framework, which remains a cornerstone of our shareholder value creation strategy. In a volatile macro environment—with WTI averaging $82 per barrel this quarter, Brent at $86, and global LNG spot prices holding firm above $12/MMBtu amid strong Asian winter demand—our priorities are clear and disciplined: first, a sustainable and growing dividend; second, opportunistic share repurchases; and third, high-return reinvestments in our core assets. This framework is underpinned by our fortress balance sheet, with net debt to EBITDA at 0.8x and $4.2 billion in liquidity, giving us the flexibility to navigate OPEC+ production cuts, geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, and the ongoing energy transition.

Our dividend policy is sacrosanct. We declared a Q4 dividend of $0.55 per share today, marking our 28th consecutive quarterly increase and bringing the full-year payout to $2.10 per share—a 10% hike from 2023. At current share prices around $70, this equates to a compelling 3.0% yield, well above our peer average of 2.4% as tracked by the Alerian MLP Index peers like Enterprise Products and our supermajor comps such as Chevron and ExxonMobil. This isn't just maintenance mode; it's backed by robust free cash flow generation. Our trailing 12-month FCF was $5.8 billion, even after $8.1 billion in capex, driven by upstream efficiencies and midstream fee-based contracts yielding 85% of EBITDA. Our payout ratio sits comfortably at 36% of FCF, leaving ample headroom versus our 50% target ceiling. We've stress-tested this at $60 WTI breakevens—our corporate average is $48/bbl—and we still cover the dividend 1.8x. Looking ahead, we expect to grow the dividend by 8-12% annually through the cycle, funded by organic cash flows from our Permian and Guyana ramps.

With dividends covered, we turn to buybacks, which enhance EPS and ROCE. Earlier this year, our Board authorized a new $4 billion open-market repurchase program, layered on top of $1.2 billion remaining from 2023. In Q3 alone, we repurchased 12.5 million shares at an average of $68, or $850 million total YTD—about 14% of our program pace. These aren't knee-jerk reactions; we execute opportunistically when shares trade below our intrinsic NAV per share, which we peg at $95 based on discounted cash flow models incorporating $75 long-term WTI and 12% WACC. Buybacks added 45 cents to adjusted EPS this quarter, and on a run-rate basis, the full program could drive $2.50+ EPS accretion by year-end 2025.

Finally, reinvestment in the business captures the highest IRR opportunities. We're guiding $8.0-8.5 billion capex for 2024, flat to last year, with 65% allocated to upstream development yielding >25% IRRs at current strips. Our returns-first mindset means no low-margin barrels: every project must clear a 15% hurdle rate and $45 WTI breakeven. Breaking it regionally: Permian Basin takes 45% of capex at $3.7 billion, where we're drilling 140 net wells in the Delaware and Midland, targeting 20%+ oil cuts via our Cube development model—stacked laterals with 12,000-ft horizontals. Q3 IP rates averaged 2,400 boe/d per well, 15% above type curve. Guyana gets 25% at $2.0 billion, with our Stabroek Block stake ramping Payara Phase 1 to 220 Mbbl/d by 2026. Gulf of Mexico & North Sea 15% at $1.2 billion for quick-cycle tie-backs. LNG & Midstream 10% at $800 million, expanding Plaquemines to 20 MTPA. Tech & Sustainability 5% at $400 million for AI reservoir sims and CCUS pilots.

Our allocation is dynamic: 40-45% of FCF to dividends/buybacks this year ($3.0B combined), 50% to growth capex, and the balance to debt reduction and bolt-ons. This has compounded TSR at 18% annualized over five years.

Before moving to operations, a quick note on realized prices, as they underpinned these results. Our realized oil price averaged $82.15 per barrel, up 8% sequentially from $76.20 in Q2 and 12% year-over-year. This compares to the NYMEX WTI benchmark at $84.50 per barrel. On natural gas, we realized $3.25 per MCF, a 15% increase from $2.82 in Q2 but flat YoY, against Henry Hub at $3.45 per MCF. These supported adjusted EBITDA of $1.2 billion, with upstream realizations over 70% of revenue.

Oil production from Permian assets benefited from WTI-Midland differential tightening to $1.25 per barrel on Matterhorn Express and EPIC Crude pipelines. Without hedges, realizations would have been $81.90 per bbl, but 65% of volumes swapped at $75 floor and 20% in three-way collars generated $1.05 per bbl uplift, or $90 million. Gas at 1.2 Bcf/d saw $0.35 premium in Haynesville but $0.45 discount on Waha; 75% hedged at $3.10 floor delivered $0.15 per MCF gain, $55 million protection. Our book has 55% of 2024 oil at $76.50 swaps, 60% gas at $3.40.

Finally, on production outlook: For Q4 2024, we guide to 465-475 thousand BOE per day, 3-6% sequential growth. Full-year 2024 midpoint at 455 thousand BOE/d, up 8% from 2023. Oil at 65% mix. Key drivers: 12 operated rigs in Permian, 45-50 Q4 completions adding 35-40k BOE/d; Eagle Ford bolt-on; GOM steady. Headwinds like turnarounds mitigated by hedging 60% oil at $75 collars.

I will now turn the call over to Mike Rodriguez for an operational update.

Mike Rodriguez: Thank you, Sarah. On the operational front, we continue to execute our strategy effectively. Our production averaged 450 thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day. We successfully brought Delaware Basin pads online, contributing significantly to growth.

Good morning, everyone. Before diving deeper, let's highlight our Q3 production volumes, the cornerstone of our free cash flow. Overall, total production hit 450 thousand BOE/d, +2.3% QoQ from 440 thousand in Q2 and +7.1% YoY from 420 thousand in Q3 2023. This from 28 new pads adding 25k BOE/d. Oil at 62% mix.

Crude oil averaged 280 thousand bbl/d, +1.8% QoQ from 275k and +7.7% YoY from 260k. Driven by Permian Delaware Wolfcamp pads with 1,800 bbl/d 30-day IPs using dissolvable diverters and 3,500 lbs proppant/ft. Permian 202 Mbbl/d, 72%; Eagle Ford 45k flat; Bakken 33k steady.

Natural gas at 1,020 MMcf/d or 170k BOE/d, +3% QoQ from 990 MMcf/d and +6.3% YoY. From Permian associated gas and Eagle Ford curtailments easing; flaring to <1%. Longer laterals at 12,500 ft yield 20-25% efficiencies; Permian 68% of BOE/d.

We're guiding Q4 to 465-475k total, oil 285-290k. This supports full-year 455k, up 8%.

We're also advancing cost reduction, with lifting costs trending down impressively. Company-wide LOE at $8.72/BOE in Q3, 30% below Q4 2021's $12.45, 14% below Q3 2023. Onshore sub-$8. Drivers: volume leverage from 22% Permian growth; cost-outs via AI predictive maintenance cutting downtime 28%; water recycling at 65% saving 22% on disposal; electrification slashing fuel 45k MMBtu/d. Permian $6.95, Eagle Ford $9.40, Bakken $10.50, GOM $18.75 improving.

Now I'll turn it over to Lisa Chen for an update on our exploration activities.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Mike. We are excited about the potential of our exploration program. We recently completed a successful seismic survey in the Namibia offshore blocks and are planning to drill 8 exploration wells in the next year. We believe these wells, including farm-down carries from TotalEnergies, have the potential to add significant reserves to our portfolio, mirroring Guyana upside.

Finally, I'll turn it over to Tom Harris to discuss our marketing strategy.

Tom Harris: Thank you, Lisa. We are focused on optimizing our marketing strategy to maximize the value of our production. We are seeing strong demand for our low-carbon LNG in the Asian market, and we are working to expand our customer base and strengthen relationships with existing customers like JERA and Shell. The impact on fee-based EBITDA is significant, now 25% of total.

I will now turn it over to Emily Green to discuss our sustainability efforts.

Emily Green: Thank you, Tom. We are committed to reducing our environmental footprint and operating in a sustainable manner. We have made significant progress on reducing our greenhouse gas emissions and are investing in renewable energy projects. We are also working to improve our water management practices and protect biodiversity.

Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. ESG is core to our long-term value at Apex. We're targeting net-zero Scope 1/2 by 2050, 40% absolute Scope 1/2 cut by 2030 from 2019 baseline, methane <0.2% by 2025, near-zero flaring by 2025, 20% Scope 3 cut by 2030.

Progress: 2023 Scope 1/2 at 41.2 MMtCO2e, 17.6% below 2019's 50.1 despite 12% production growth; intensity 19.8 kg/boe vs 25.4, YTD on pace for 18.9. Methane 0.18% in 2023, 64% below 2019 via 1,200 monitors, AI from Bridger Photonics, 15k leaks fixed. Flaring 92% down to 8.2 MMscf/d via Permian gathering.

Regional: Permian intensity 16.5 kg/boe, 40% rig electrification; Guyana 18% cut via turbine upgrades; North Sea 14% via CCUS; Middle East zero flaring. CCUS Polaris Hub 1.2 MMtCO2e/yr scaling to 5 MMt; 60% GOM electrification; H2 blends in Bakken.

Efficiency saved $180M in 2023; 'A' MSCI rating cut debt costs 25 bps. $3.5B low-carbon capex to 2027 for CCUS, AI, 1 GW renewables. 2nd quartile in Wood Mackenzie index.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Brian Miller with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Brian Miller: Good morning. Can you provide more detail on debt levels and leverage trajectory?

Sarah Jenkins: Absolutely, Brian. As I detailed earlier, total debt at $14.8B, net $12.3B, 2.4x net debt/EBITDA targeting below 2.0x by YE25. Refinancings lowered costs to 4.6%, maturities extended. Permian FCF driving paydowns.

Operator: Our next question comes from Alex Patel with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Alex Patel: Good morning. What are your expectations for production guidance next quarter and full year?

Sarah Jenkins: For Q4, 465-475k BOE/d; full-year midpoint 455k, up 8%. Driven by Permian rigs, completions; mitigated by hedging and turnarounds.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sarah Jenkins with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins: Thanks. Good morning, team. I wanted to dive into your lifting costs per BOE. You've highlighted some impressive declines—could you walk us through the trend analysis and the key cost reduction initiatives driving that, with some regional color if possible?

Sarah Jenkins: Absolutely, Sarah. Great question. Company-wide LOE $8.72/BOE in Q3, 30% off 2021 peaks, 14% YoY down. Onshore sub-$8. Volumes leverage 40%, cost-outs 35%. AI maintenance cut downtime 28%, water recycling 65% saved 22%, electrification $0.65/BOE. Permian $6.95, Eagle Ford $9.40 improving. On track for $7.50-7.75 by 2025.

Operator: Our next question comes from Chris Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Chris Lee: How will the results of the exploration program affect the company's future strategy?

Lisa Chen: The Namibia seismic and 8 wells planned will diversify reserves, adding Guyana-like upside without leverage. Enhances inventory life to 15+ years, funding organic growth.

Operator: Our next question comes from Dana Wong with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Dana Wong: What is the outlook for the low-carbon LNG product in the coming years?

Tom Harris: Strong, with Plaquemines expansion to 20 MTPA by 2027, 15-year offtakes. Premiums 5-10% in Europe, hedging volatility; 25% EBITDA now.

Operator: Our next question comes from Rob Kim with Citi. Please go ahead.

Rob Kim: Could you elaborate on your sustainability targets?

Emily Green: Net-zero 2050, 40% Scope 1/2 by 2030, methane 0.2% by 2025. Ahead: intensity down 22%, methane 0.18%, flaring 92% cut. $3.5B capex accelerating CCUS, electrification.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to David Thompson for closing remarks.

David Thompson: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q3 2024. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
